chunks: My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, from Yazīd ibn ‘Umar ibn Ťalḥah, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said, while he was in Ḥīrah: 'Do you not want that which I promised you?' I said, 'Yes,' meaning going to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him). He said, so he rode, and his son Ismā’īl rode with him, and I rode with them. Until when he passed Thawiyyah, and it was between Ḥīrah and Najaf near some white gravel, he dismounted, and Ismā’īl dismounted, and I dismounted with them. So he prayed, and Ismā’īl prayed, and I prayed. Then he said to Ismā’īl, 'Stand and say Salām to your grandfather, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (peace be upon him).' So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Is Ḥusain (peace be upon him) not in Karbalā?' He said, 'Yes. However, when his head was carried to Shām, a servant of ours stole it and buried it next to the Commander of the Believers.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Belieeners, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الثَّوِيَّة: Thawiyyah, a location between Hira and Najaf
key_terms.الشَّام: Sham (Syria), where the head was being transported
key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Hira, a city in Iraq near Najaf
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Servant or freed slave, referring to a follower of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Where is the grave of the head of Imam Ali located according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia tradition of the 'Head of Imam Ali' being interred in al-Hirah, distinct from the main body in Karbala, a view supported by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid. It underscores the spiritual significance of al-Hirah as a sacred site for ziyarah, linking the Prophet's family directly to the region of Iraq. The account also illustrates the Imams' personal connection to their ancestors through shared prayer and visitation rituals.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb both narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, from Yazīd ibn ‘Umar ibn Ťalḥah, who said:

When Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) was in Ḥīrah, he asked me, “Do you not want that which I promised you?” “Yes,” I replied – he meant going to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.). Then the Imam rode his sumpter. His son, Ismā’īl, and I accompanied him. We passed Thawiyyah and then stopped between Ḥīrah and Najaf next to some white-coloured gravel. Imam (a.s.) and his son, Ismā’īl, descended their sumpters, so I descended my sumpter. We (all) prayed. Then Imam (a.s.) said to Ismā’īl, “Stand and say Salām to your grandfather, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.).” So I asked, “May I sacrifice myself for you! Is Ḥusain (a.s.) not in Karbalā?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes. However, when his head was being carried to Shām, one of our servants stole it and buried it next to the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).”
